evidence.quote: We have seen considerable progress in lowering inflation since early 2023, but progress seems to have stalled in recent months.
I see greater risks to the price stability side of our mandate, especially while the labor market remains near full employment
I would prefer to proceed cautiously in bringing the policy rate down to better assess how far we are from the end point
My estimate of the neutral policy rate is much higher than it was before the pandemic, and therefore we may be closer to a neutral policy stance than we currently think.
The real economy continues to be strong, with solid momentum in economic activity, robust household spending and business investment, and a healthy labor market that remains near full employment.

parsed.rationale: Bowman stresses stalled disinflation, upside inflation risks, a strong economy, and a high neutral rate, favoring slow, cautious cuts. Much of the speech concerns bank regulation, but the monetary policy portion is clearly hawkish-leaning.
